name: Primary Basilar Invagination

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Basilar Invagination

criteria.description: Posterior displacement of the odontoid process above Chamberlain's line on lateral skull radiograph or CT
Reduced clivus-canal angle (<135 degrees) on sagittal imaging indicating brainstem compression
Presence of neurological signs consistent with cervicomedullary compression such as spasticity or cranial nerve deficits

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological evidence of odontoid displacement above Chamberlain's line plus clinical or imaging signs of brainstem or cervical cord compression
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities such as CT and MRI; clinical correlation is essential.

imaging: Posterior displacement of odontoid process above Chamberlain's line on lateral skull radiograph or CT
Reduced clivus-canal angle on sagittal MRI
Compression of cervicomedullary junction on MRI
other: Clinical signs of upper motor neuron lesion
Cranial nerve deficits consistent with brainstem compression

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with underlying bone disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis or Paget disease
Often presents later in life with known predisposing conditions
Herniation of cerebellar tonsils below foramen magnum
Absence of odontoid displacement above Chamberlain's line

redFlags: Signs of brainstem compression such as respiratory compromise
Sudden onset of cranial nerve palsies
references: Goel A. Basilar invagination: a review. Neurol India. 2014;62(4): 351-360.
Chamberlain WE. Basilar impression (Platybasia): a summary of 30 cases. Radiology. 1939;32(3): 337-361.
Kumar R, et al. Imaging features of basilar invagination and its clinical significance. J Clin Neurosci. 2017;44: 1-7.
